chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who gave charity on behalf of his children who have reached maturity, he said: 'If they do not take possession of it before he dies, it is inheritance. And if he gives charity on behalf of those who have not reached maturity from his children, it is valid, because the father is the one who manages their affairs.' And he said: 'He does not have the right to reclaim the charity if he gave it seeking the Face of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a father giving charity on behalf of his adult and minor children?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *hibah* (gift) and *sadaqah* (charity) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that possession (*qabd*) is the critical factor in determining ownership transfer. It establishes that while a father retains control over the assets of his minor children, voluntary charity given for the sake of Allah is irrevocable, reflecting the principle of *ikhlās* (sincerity) in charitable acts. This ruling is foundational in *Fiqh al-Ja'fari* for resolving disputes regarding inheritance and gift revocation.
